description: Dialogue fragments, some of which require the other speaker's line to make sense and should be rejected, alongside standalone remarks that hold up on their own.
sourceText: "Why do you keep going back there," she asked, "when it only ever disappoints you?" He shrugged before answering. "Because hope, once you have tasted it, is very hard to give up entirely, even when the evidence says you should." She said nothing for a while, watching the rain against the window. "That may be the most honest thing you have said to me all year," she finally replied, and neither of them spoke again until the storm had passed completely.
